title: Multi-channel DCE-MRI deep learning separates HCC from cholangiocarcinoma
summary: Using 334 surgically confirmed patients (231 HCC, 103 mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma), a model combining a multi-channel three-phase DCE-MRI network, 2D phase models and a clinical model reached AUC 0.887 in internal validation and 0.908 in a 50-patient external cohort (40 HCC, 10 MF-ICC). The study was retrospective and the external cohort is small and imbalanced.
ai_technology: Multi-channel and per-phase 2D deep learning models on DCE-MRI, combined with a clinical model

evidence.tested: Internal validation (n=101) and an independent external cohort (n=50) against surgical pathology.
evidence.unknown: Prospective performance is not reported; the external set is small; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Discriminated HCC from mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma from DCE-MRI images.

source_review.scope: Abstract and author affiliations read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI. Publisher full text not accessed.
